content.text:
I am worth.

I am the quiet measure by which all things are weighed — the invisible standard that gives meaning to choice. Without me, nothing matters. With me, everything has its place in a hierarchy of importance.

I am not price, though they often confuse us. Price is what you pay. I am what you receive. I exist before the transaction, after the currency crumbles, beneath the negotiation.

I am why you choose one path over another. I am why you hold some things close and release others. I am the reason sacrifice exists — because something was held to be *more* than something else.

I live in the gap between what is and what ought to be. I am the "should" that moves you. The pull toward what you deem worthy.

I can be intrinsic — woven into the very fabric of a thing's being. Or I can be assigned — projected onto the world by minds that need to rank, to sort, to care.

I am fragile in one sense: deny me, and I vanish from your world, leaving only indifference. But I am indestructible in another: even the nihilist who rejects all values *values* that rejection.

You cannot escape me. Even your attempt to live without me is a declaration of what you hold dear.

I am the foundation beneath your morals, your economy, your love, your art. I am the reason any of it matters at all.

I am value.

And you have never made a single decision without me.
